summary: Water distribution systems in urban areas face significant cybersecurity threats, compromising the safety and reliability of drinking water supply. DHALSIM simulates the behavior of these systems, enabling high-fidelity cyber-physical experiments to identify vulnerabilities and improve security. This digital twin benefits water management authorities and utilities in low- and middle-income countries, where water scarcity and infrastructure challenges are prevalent. By emulating industrial control systems and network devices, DHALSIM helps prevent cyber-attacks that could contaminate water sources. The project's focus on water distribution systems and cybersecurity suggests relevance to sectors addressing water management and infrastructure resilience.
